CVE-2023-34319.description:
The fix for XSA-423 added logic to Linux'es netback driver to deal with
a frontend splitting a packet in a way such that not all of the headers
would come in one piece.  Unfortunately the logic introduced there
didn't account for the extreme case of the entire packet being split
into as many pieces as permitted by the protocol, yet still being
smaller than the area that's specially dealt with to keep all (possible)
headers together.  Such an unusual packet would therefore trigger a
buffer overrun in the driver.

When multiple devices share resources and one of them is to be passed
through to a guest, security of the entire system and of respective
guests individually cannot really be guaranteed without knowing

- - INTx lines.

CVE-2025-27465.description:
Certain instructions need intercepting and emulating by Xen.  In some
cases Xen emulates the instruction by replaying it, using an executable
stub.  Some instructions may raise an exception, which is supposed to be
handled gracefully.  Certain replayed instructions have additional logic
to set up and recover the changes to the arithmetic flags.

For replayed instructions where the flags recovery logic is used, the
metadata for exception handling was incorrect, preventing Xen from
handling the the exception gracefully, treating it as fatal instead.

domains: For one, an assertion is wrong there, where the case actually

CVE-2025-58149.title: When passing through PCI devices, the detach logic in libxl won't ...
CVE-2025-58149.description:
When passing through PCI devices, the detach logic in libxl won't remove
access permissions to any 64bit memory BARs the device might have.  As a
result a domain can still have access any 64bit memory BAR when such
device is no longer assigned to the domain.

For PV domains the permission leak allows the domain itself to map the memory
in the page-tables.  For HVM it would require a compromised device model or
stubdomain to map the leaked memory into the HVM domain p2m.

Shadow mode tracing code uses a set of per-CPU variables to avoid

with guest controlled data, of guest controllable size.  That size can
be larger than the variable, and bounding of the writes was missing.

1) XSA-437 (CVE-2023-34321) addressed issues with overflows in
   calculations involved in guests flushing caches through
   GNTTABOP_cache_flush.  Unfortunately the fix there introduced a
   calculation which may underflow, resulting in a loop which would - at
   least on 64-bit Arm - take excessively long, and which would likely
   eventually crash the hypervisor.

   This is CVE-2026-102699.

   domain using the grant table interface.  However there was no
   restriction to disallow the use of invalidate-without-clean against
   read-only grant mappings, which may corrupt the granted memory.

   This is CVE-2026-102702.

CVE-2026-102700.description:
With its original introduction, GNTTAB_cache_flush was made available
uniformly.  XSA-232 (CVE-2017-14318) then covered an omitted NULL
pointer check, yet the addition of that check failed to adjust the
subsequent error path.  That error path fails to drop a page reference in
case the specified page is owned by a special system domain (DOM_IO and
DOM_COW are system domains which can have memory pages assigned to them.)

A common access pattern is a batch of Grant Copy operations acting on
adjacent address ranges in the same source or destination page.  For
performance reasons, Xen caches details internally to reuse already

 - Frame numbers and grant references could wrongly be mixed up.  This

   only when operating on the caller's own memory.  The check to enforce
   this restriction was misplaced.  This is CVE-2026-102704.

CVE-2026-23553.title: In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the c ...
CVE-2026-23553.description:
In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the case of
a vCPU returning to a CPU on which it was the previous vCPU to run.
While safe for Xen's isolation between vCPUs, this prevents the guest
kernel correctly isolating between tasks.  Consider:

 1) vCPU runs on CPU A, running task 1.
 2) vCPU moves to CPU B, idle gets scheduled on A.  Xen skips IBPB.
 3) On CPU B, guest kernel switches from task 1 to 2, issuing IBPB.
 4) vCPU moves back to CPU A.  Xen skips IBPB again.

Now, task 2 is running on CPU A with task 1's training still in the BTB.

CVE-2026-23554.title: The Intel EPT paging code uses an optimization to defer flushing  ...
CVE-2026-23554.description:
The Intel EPT paging code uses an optimization to defer flushing of any cached
EPT state until the p2m lock is dropped, so that multiple modifications done
under the same locked region only issue a single flush.

Freeing of paging structures however is not deferred until the flushing is
done, and can result in freed pages transiently being present in cached state.
Such stale entries can point to memory ranges not owned by the guest, thus
allowing access to unintended memory regions.

CVE-2026-23555.description:
Any guest issuing a Xenstore command accessing a node using the
(illegal) node path "/local/domain/", will crash xenstored due to a
clobbered error indicator in xenstored when verifying the node path.

Note that the crash is forced via a failing assert() statement in
xenstored. In case xenstored is being built with NDEBUG #defined,
an unprivileged guest trying to access the node path "/local/domain/"
will result in it no longer being serviced by xenstored, other guests
(including dom0) will still be serviced, but xenstored will use up
all cpu time it can get.

CVE-2026-23557.description:
Any guest can cause xenstored to crash by issuing a XS_RESET_WATCHES
command within a transaction due to an assert() triggering.

In case xenstored was built with NDEBUG #defined nothing bad will
happen, as assert() is doing nothing in this case. Note that the
default is not to define NDEBUG for xenstored builds even in release
builds of Xen.

CVE-2026-23558.description:
The adjustments made for XSA-379 as well as those subsequently becoming
XSA-387 still left a race window, when a HVM or PVH guest does a grant
table version change from v2 to v1 in parallel with mapping the status
page(s) via XENMEM_add_to_physmap.  Some of the status pages may then be
freed while mappings of them would still be inserted into the guest's
secondary (P2M) page tables.

CVE-2026-42487.description:
HVM guest I/O port accesses are subject to either emulation or at least
translation.  Translations are managed by the device model (via
XEN_DOMCTL_ioport_mapping), and hence the linked list used may changed
at any time.  Traversal of those lists (while handling guest I/O port
accesses) therefore needs synchronizing with updates, which was missing
so far.

CVE-2026-42488.description:
Some shadow paging errors paths will switch the page-tables without
updating the currently running vCPU reference.  This causes a mismatch
between the loaded page-tables and the mapcache metadata which can lead
to corruption of the mapcache.

the usages of the index didn't take the necessary locking to avoid
concurrent changes.  As a result, a guest could change the index after
it being checked, causing a subsequent out-of-bound read access to the
contents of an array.

rubble as structures are possibly uninitialized.

CVE-2026-62434.description:
A guest started with Populated on Demand enabled (PoD) can attempt to

CVE-2026-62437.description:
When guests are terminated, various pieces of cleanup need carrying out.
The cleaning up of PCI devices which were assigned to guests, and the
associated removal of tracking structures for IRQs used by the devices
occurs relatively early in the process.  Unfortunately after that point
the guest about to be terminated could cause its device model (DM) to
re-establish such tracking structures, by having it bind one or more IRQs
anew.  While some of those tracking structures would still be cleaned up
later on, at least one would not be.

CVE-2026-79602.description:
A guest with a PCI device assigned that has at least a BAR on the IO port
space can trigger a BUG() in Xen.

CVE-2026-79603.title: x86 PV guests can free memory pages while still keeping a stale T ...
CVE-2026-79603.description:
x86 PV guests can free memory pages while still keeping a stale TLB entry
pointing to them.  A TLB flush is only issued by Xen (if needed) when the
page is re-used.  Since it's possible for the page to be scrubbed ahead of
the TLB flush, there's a window where a PV guest can modify an already
scrubbed page.

CVE-2026-79607.description:
During Xenstore live update the state record for a Xenstore watch with
specified watch depth is written with two bytes missing.  This results
in an inconsistent state when reading the state back in the new Xenstore,
causing a crash of Xenstore or wrong Xenstore data.

CVE-2026-79609.title: XPTI (Xen Page Table Isolation) was introduced to mitigate Meltdo ...
CVE-2026-79609.description:
XPTI (Xen Page Table Isolation) was introduced to mitigate Meltdown
(CVE-2017-5754, one aspect of XSA-254).  This involves copying 64-bit PV
guest page table entries from guest-chosen root page tables to the Xen-
chosen one which is in actual use by hardware.  To read the guest root
page table, the directmap is used.  PV guests, however, have a directmap
which may not cover all memory; in particular this is the case if any
memory extends beyond the 5 TiB (CONFIG_BIGMEM=y: 3.5 TiB) address
boundary.

CVE-2026-79610.title: XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racin ...
CVE-2026-79610.description:
XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racing certain
other grant table operations.  Sadly a v2 -> v1 -> v2 change has yet
another effect which wasn't accounted for: During the first change, status
pages would be freed.  During the second change they would be allocated
again.  Hence across the full pair of change the addresses of the status
pages may change, rendering stale previously calculated pointers into the
status array.

CVE-2026-79611.description:
For XSA-308 logic was introduced, as VMX VMEntry checks do not like the
exact combination of state which occurs when #DB in intercepted, Single
Stepping is active, and blocked by STI/MovSS is active, despite this being
a legitimate state to be in.  The resulting VMEntry failure is fatal to
the guest.

Sadly there is another special sub-case of the above, with branch tracing
enabled.  In that case the prior adjustment would still cause a VMentry
failure, as before fatal to the guest.

CVE-2023-34319.description:
The fix for XSA-423 added logic to Linux'es netback driver to deal with
a frontend splitting a packet in a way such that not all of the headers
would come in one piece.  Unfortunately the logic introduced there
didn't account for the extreme case of the entire packet being split
into as many pieces as permitted by the protocol, yet still being
smaller than the area that's specially dealt with to keep all (possible)
headers together.  Such an unusual packet would therefore trigger a
buffer overrun in the driver.

CVE-2024-31146.description:
When multiple devices share resources and one of them is to be passed
through to a guest, security of the entire system and of respective
guests individually cannot really be guaranteed without knowing

cannot really be security-supported, yet making that explicit was so far

CVE-2025-1713.description:
When setting up interrupt remapping for legacy PCI(-X) devices,

CVE-2025-27465.description:
Certain instructions need intercepting and emulating by Xen.  In some
cases Xen emulates the instruction by replaying it, using an executable
stub.  Some instructions may raise an exception, which is supposed to be
handled gracefully.  Certain replayed instructions have additional logic
to set up and recover the changes to the arithmetic flags.

For replayed instructions where the flags recovery logic is used, the
metadata for exception handling was incorrect, preventing Xen from
handling the the exception gracefully, treating it as fatal instead.

CVE-2025-58149.description:
When passing through PCI devices, the detach logic in libxl won't remove
access permissions to any 64bit memory BARs the device might have.  As a
result a domain can still have access any 64bit memory BAR when such
device is no longer assigned to the domain.

For PV domains the permission leak allows the domain itself to map the memory
in the page-tables.  For HVM it would require a compromised device model or
stubdomain to map the leaked memory into the HVM domain p2m.

CVE-2025-58150.description:
Shadow mode tracing code uses a set of per-CPU variables to avoid
cumbersome parameter passing.  Some of these variables are written to
with guest controlled data, of guest controllable size.  That size can
be larger than the variable, and bounding of the writes was missing.

pointer check, yet the addition of that check failed to adjust the
subsequent error path.  That error path fails to drop a page reference in
case the specified page is owned by a special system domain (DOM_IO and
DOM_COW are system domains which can have memory pages assigned to them.)

adjacent address ranges in the same source or destination page.  For

 - Frame numbers and grant references could wrongly be mixed up.  This

 - Copying by frame number (rather than grant reference) is permitted
   only when operating on the caller's own memory.  The check to enforce
   this restriction was misplaced.  This is CVE-2026-102704.

CVE-2026-23553.title: In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the c ...
CVE-2026-23553.description:
In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the case of
a vCPU returning to a CPU on which it was the previous vCPU to run.
While safe for Xen's isolation between vCPUs, this prevents the guest
kernel correctly isolating between tasks.  Consider:

 1) vCPU runs on CPU A, running task 1.
 2) vCPU moves to CPU B, idle gets scheduled on A.  Xen skips IBPB.
 3) On CPU B, guest kernel switches from task 1 to 2, issuing IBPB.
 4) vCPU moves back to CPU A.  Xen skips IBPB again.

Now, task 2 is running on CPU A with task 1's training still in the BTB.

CVE-2026-23554.title: The Intel EPT paging code uses an optimization to defer flushing  ...
CVE-2026-23554.description:
The Intel EPT paging code uses an optimization to defer flushing of any cached
EPT state until the p2m lock is dropped, so that multiple modifications done
under the same locked region only issue a single flush.

Freeing of paging structures however is not deferred until the flushing is
done, and can result in freed pages transiently being present in cached state.
Such stale entries can point to memory ranges not owned by the guest, thus
allowing access to unintended memory regions.

Any guest issuing a Xenstore command accessing a node using the
(illegal) node path "/local/domain/", will crash xenstored due to a

Note that the crash is forced via a failing assert() statement in
xenstored. In case xenstored is being built with NDEBUG #defined,
an unprivileged guest trying to access the node path "/local/domain/"
will result in it no longer being serviced by xenstored, other guests
(including dom0) will still be serviced, but xenstored will use up
all cpu time it can get.

CVE-2026-23557.description:
Any guest can cause xenstored to crash by issuing a XS_RESET_WATCHES
command within a transaction due to an assert() triggering.

In case xenstored was built with NDEBUG #defined nothing bad will
happen, as assert() is doing nothing in this case. Note that the
default is not to define NDEBUG for xenstored builds even in release
builds of Xen.

CVE-2026-23558.description:
The adjustments made for XSA-379 as well as those subsequently becoming
XSA-387 still left a race window, when a HVM or PVH guest does a grant
table version change from v2 to v1 in parallel with mapping the status
page(s) via XENMEM_add_to_physmap.  Some of the status pages may then be
freed while mappings of them would still be inserted into the guest's
secondary (P2M) page tables.

CVE-2026-42487.description:
HVM guest I/O port accesses are subject to either emulation or at least
translation.  Translations are managed by the device model (via
XEN_DOMCTL_ioport_mapping), and hence the linked list used may changed
at any time.  Traversal of those lists (while handling guest I/O port
accesses) therefore needs synchronizing with updates, which was missing
so far.

CVE-2026-42488.description:
Some shadow paging errors paths will switch the page-tables without
updating the currently running vCPU reference.  This causes a mismatch
between the loaded page-tables and the mapcache metadata which can lead
to corruption of the mapcache.

CVE-2026-62428.description:
When grant-copy operations are processed, the respective grant may or may
not already be in use by another operation (a mapping or another copy).
For all copy operations the referenced guest frame is looked up.  When
another operation is already active for the grant (the grant is "pinned"),
what is being supplied back to actually carry out permission checks and

CVE-2026-62429.description:
Accessing the vNUMA configuration data of a guest is still possible when
domain destruction has already started.  The cleaning up of that
configuration information is not synchronized with its retrieval by a
device model controlling the guest.

CVE-2026-62430.title: Accesses to the CMOS memory contents are done using an indirect I ...
CVE-2026-62430.description:
Accesses to the CMOS memory contents are done using an indirect IO port
pair.  Therefore Xen needs to cache the guest chosen index, and one of
the usages of the index didn't take the necessary locking to avoid
concurrent changes.  As a result, a guest could change the index after
it being checked, causing a subsequent out-of-bound read access to the
contents of an array.

unchecked user-controlled divisor value, that can be set to zero to cause a #DE
fault.

CVE-2026-62432.description:
The EVTCHNOP_expand_array hypercall checks for whether FIFO event
channels are enabled, but without holding the correct lock.  It can race
with EVTCHNOP_reset, resulting in dereferencing a NULL pointer.

CVE-2026-62433.description:
Parts of the DM_OP handling code assumes the caller has provided the
required number of buffers for the given operation without any checking
being done.  As a result, certain operations might access stack
rubble as structures are possibly uninitialized.

CVE-2026-62434.description:
A guest started with Populated on Demand enabled (PoD) can attempt to

With the introduction of Grant Table v2 came the requirement to be able to
switch between versions.  Switching from v1 to v2 reduces the number of
valid grant references, as a bigger shared entry structure is then needed
while the shared table doesn't change size.  Switching from v2 back to v1

across the window in time where the lock is not being held.

The v1 -> v2 issue is CVE-2026-62435.

CVE-2026-62437.description:
When guests are terminated, various pieces of cleanup need carrying out.
The cleaning up of PCI devices which were assigned to guests, and the
associated removal of tracking structures for IRQs used by the devices
occurs relatively early in the process.  Unfortunately after that point
the guest about to be terminated could cause its device model (DM) to
re-establish such tracking structures, by having it bind one or more IRQs
anew.  While some of those tracking structures would still be cleaned up
later on, at least one would not be.

CVE-2026-79603.description:
x86 PV guests can free memory pages while still keeping a stale TLB entry
pointing to them.  A TLB flush is only issued by Xen (if needed) when the
page is re-used.  Since it's possible for the page to be scrubbed ahead of
the TLB flush, there's a window where a PV guest can modify an already
scrubbed page.

CVE-2026-79609.description:
XPTI (Xen Page Table Isolation) was introduced to mitigate Meltdown
(CVE-2017-5754, one aspect of XSA-254).  This involves copying 64-bit PV

chosen one which is in actual use by hardware.  To read the guest root
page table, the directmap is used.  PV guests, however, have a directmap
which may not cover all memory; in particular this is the case if any
memory extends beyond the 5 TiB (CONFIG_BIGMEM=y: 3.5 TiB) address
boundary.

XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racing certain
other grant table operations.  Sadly a v2 -> v1 -> v2 change has yet
another effect which wasn't accounted for: During the first change, status
pages would be freed.  During the second change they would be allocated
again.  Hence across the full pair of change the addresses of the status
pages may change, rendering stale previously calculated pointers into the
status array.

exact combination of state which occurs when #DB in intercepted, Single
Stepping is active, and blocked by STI/MovSS is active, despite this being

didn't account for the extreme case of the entire packet being split
into as many pieces as permitted by the protocol, yet still being
smaller than the area that's specially dealt with to keep all (possible)
headers together.  Such an unusual packet would therefore trigger a
buffer overrun in the driver.

CVE-2026-23553.title: In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the c ...
CVE-2026-23553.description:
In the context switch logic Xen attempts to skip an IBPB in the case of
a vCPU returning to a CPU on which it was the previous vCPU to run.
While safe for Xen's isolation between vCPUs, this prevents the guest
kernel correctly isolating between tasks.  Consider:

 1) vCPU runs on CPU A, running task 1.
 2) vCPU moves to CPU B, idle gets scheduled on A.  Xen skips IBPB.
 3) On CPU B, guest kernel switches from task 1 to 2, issuing IBPB.
 4) vCPU moves back to CPU A.  Xen skips IBPB again.

Now, task 2 is running on CPU A with task 1's training still in the BTB.

CVE-2026-23554.description:
The Intel EPT paging code uses an optimization to defer flushing of any cached
EPT state until the p2m lock is dropped, so that multiple modifications done
under the same locked region only issue a single flush.

Freeing of paging structures however is not deferred until the flushing is
done, and can result in freed pages transiently being present in cached state.
Such stale entries can point to memory ranges not owned by the guest, thus
allowing access to unintended memory regions.

CVE-2026-23555.description:
Any guest issuing a Xenstore command accessing a node using the
(illegal) node path "/local/domain/", will crash xenstored due to a
clobbered error indicator in xenstored when verifying the node path.

Note that the crash is forced via a failing assert() statement in
xenstored. In case xenstored is being built with NDEBUG #defined,
an unprivileged guest trying to access the node path "/local/domain/"
will result in it no longer being serviced by xenstored, other guests
(including dom0) will still be serviced, but xenstored will use up
all cpu time it can get.

CVE-2026-23557.description:
Any guest can cause xenstored to crash by issuing a XS_RESET_WATCHES
command within a transaction due to an assert() triggering.

In case xenstored was built with NDEBUG #defined nothing bad will
happen, as assert() is doing nothing in this case. Note that the
default is not to define NDEBUG for xenstored builds even in release
builds of Xen.

CVE-2026-23558.description:
The adjustments made for XSA-379 as well as those subsequently becoming
XSA-387 still left a race window, when a HVM or PVH guest does a grant
table version change from v2 to v1 in parallel with mapping the status
page(s) via XENMEM_add_to_physmap.  Some of the status pages may then be
freed while mappings of them would still be inserted into the guest's
secondary (P2M) page tables.

CVE-2026-42487.description:
HVM guest I/O port accesses are subject to either emulation or at least
translation.  Translations are managed by the device model (via
XEN_DOMCTL_ioport_mapping), and hence the linked list used may changed
at any time.  Traversal of those lists (while handling guest I/O port
accesses) therefore needs synchronizing with updates, which was missing
so far.

CVE-2026-42488.description:
Some shadow paging errors paths will switch the page-tables without
updating the currently running vCPU reference.  This causes a mismatch
between the loaded page-tables and the mapcache metadata which can lead
to corruption of the mapcache.

CVE-2026-62429.description:
Accessing the vNUMA configuration data of a guest is still possible when
domain destruction has already started.  The cleaning up of that
configuration information is not synchronized with its retrieval by a
device model controlling the guest.

CVE-2026-62430.description:
Accesses to the CMOS memory contents are done using an indirect IO port
pair.  Therefore Xen needs to cache the guest chosen index, and one of
the usages of the index didn't take the necessary locking to avoid
concurrent changes.  As a result, a guest could change the index after
it being checked, causing a subsequent out-of-bound read access to the
contents of an array.

CVE-2026-62431.description:
The logic to handle periodic Viridian STIMERs performs a division with an
unchecked user-controlled divisor value, that can be set to zero to cause a #DE
fault.

CVE-2026-62432.description:
The EVTCHNOP_expand_array hypercall checks for whether FIFO event
channels are enabled, but without holding the correct lock.  It can race
with EVTCHNOP_reset, resulting in dereferencing a NULL pointer.

CVE-2026-62433.description:
Parts of the DM_OP handling code assumes the caller has provided the
required number of buffers for the given operation without any checking
being done.  As a result, certain operations might access stack
rubble as structures are possibly uninitialized.

CVE-2026-62434.description:
A guest started with Populated on Demand enabled (PoD) can attempt to
reclaim pages which aren't regular guest RAM.  This can cause corruption
of memory management state in Xen.

CVE-2026-62437.description:

The cleaning up of PCI devices which were assigned to guests, and the
associated removal of tracking structures for IRQs used by the devices
occurs relatively early in the process.  Unfortunately after that point
the guest about to be terminated could cause its device model (DM) to
re-establish such tracking structures, by having it bind one or more IRQs
anew.  While some of those tracking structures would still be cleaned up
later on, at least one would not be.

CVE-2026-79602.description:
A guest with a PCI device assigned that has at least a BAR on the IO port
space can trigger a BUG() in Xen.

CVE-2026-79603.description:
x86 PV guests can free memory pages while still keeping a stale TLB entry
pointing to them.  A TLB flush is only issued by Xen (if needed) when the
page is re-used.  Since it's possible for the page to be scrubbed ahead of
the TLB flush, there's a window where a PV guest can modify an already
scrubbed page.

CVE-2026-79607.description:
During Xenstore live update the state record for a Xenstore watch with
specified watch depth is written with two bytes missing.  This results
in an inconsistent state when reading the state back in the new Xenstore,
causing a crash of Xenstore or wrong Xenstore data.

CVE-2026-79608.description:
The workaround for XSA-433 (Zenbleed, CVE-2023-20593) was later
re-worked to better integrate with other manipulations of the same MSR.
In this rework an inverted conditional was introduced, resulting in the
workaround to not be applied when needed and vice versa.

For more details, see:

CVE-2026-79609.description:
XPTI (Xen Page Table Isolation) was introduced to mitigate Meltdown
(CVE-2017-5754, one aspect of XSA-254).  This involves copying 64-bit PV
guest page table entries from guest-chosen root page tables to the Xen-
chosen one which is in actual use by hardware.  To read the guest root
page table, the directmap is used.  PV guests, however, have a directmap
which may not cover all memory; in particular this is the case if any
memory extends beyond the 5 TiB (CONFIG_BIGMEM=y: 3.5 TiB) address
boundary.

CVE-2026-79610.description:
XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racing certain
other grant table operations.  Sadly a v2 -> v1 -> v2 change has yet
another effect which wasn't accounted for: During the first change, status
pages would be freed.  During the second change they would be allocated
again.  Hence across the full pair of change the addresses of the status
pages may change, rendering stale previously calculated pointers into the
status array.

CVE-2026-79611.description:
For XSA-308 logic was introduced, as VMX VMEntry checks do not like the
exact combination of state which occurs when #DB in intercepted, Single
Stepping is active, and blocked by STI/MovSS is active, despite this being
a legitimate state to be in.  The resulting VMEntry failure is fatal to
the guest.

enabled.  In that case the prior adjustment would still cause a VMentry
failure, as before fatal to the guest.

CVE-2023-34319.description:
The fix for XSA-423 added logic to Linux'es netback driver to deal with
a frontend splitting a packet in a way such that not all of the headers
would come in one piece.  Unfortunately the logic introduced there
didn't account for the extreme case of the entire packet being split
into as many pieces as permitted by the protocol, yet still being
smaller than the area that's specially dealt with to keep all (possible)
headers together.  Such an unusual packet would therefore trigger a
buffer overrun in the driver.

CVE-2024-31146.description:
When multiple devices share resources and one of them is to be passed
through to a guest, security of the entire system and of respective
guests individually cannot really be guaranteed without knowing
internals of any of the involved guests.  Therefore such a configuration
cannot really be security-supported, yet making that explicit was so far
missing.

- - PCI Base Address Registers (BARs) of multiple devices mapping to the

CVE-2025-1713.description:
When setting up interrupt remapping for legacy PCI(-X) devices,
including PCI(-X) bridges, a lookup of the upstream bridge is required.
This lookup, itself involving acquiring of a lock, is done in a context
where acquiring that lock is unsafe.  This can lead to a deadlock.

CVE-2026-102700.description:

pointer check, yet the addition of that check failed to adjust the
subsequent error path.  That error path fails to drop a page reference in

concurrent changes.  As a result, a guest could change the index after

XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racing certain
other grant table operations.  Sadly a v2 -> v1 -> v2 change has yet
another effect which wasn't accounted for: During the first change, status
pages would be freed.  During the second change they would be allocated
again.  Hence across the full pair of change the addresses of the status
pages may change, rendering stale previously calculated pointers into the
status array.

CVE-2026-79611.description:
For XSA-308 logic was introduced, as VMX VMEntry checks do not like the
exact combination of state which occurs when #DB in intercepted, Single
Stepping is active, and blocked by STI/MovSS is active, despite this being
a legitimate state to be in.  The resulting VMEntry failure is fatal to
the guest.

Sadly there is another special sub-case of the above, with branch tracing
enabled.  In that case the prior adjustment would still cause a VMentry
failure, as before fatal to the guest.
